reconcile.note: Gill traces the porters' one-person gap to deaths and late arrivals shifting a family's headcount between the Babylon and Jerusalem registers, even where names match.

discrepancy.note: Paine observes that Nehemiah's registry differs from Ezra's in its particulars, the same defect underlying the six porter families' 139-vs-138 mismatch.

quotes.text: Nehemiah, in like manner, gives a list of the returned families, and of the number of each family. He begins as in Ezra, by saying (vii. 8): "The children of Parosh, two thousand three hundred and seventy-two;" and so on through all the families. (The list differs in several of the particulars from that of Ezra.)
quotes.attr: Thomas Paine (d. 1809), The Age of Reason, Part II (1795), ch. I, on Ezra 2:42 and Nehemiah 7:45.
